chunks: Al-Hakim Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sawli quoted on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Isma’il, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Al-Abbas that Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha’ (peace be upon him) narrated on the authority of his father (peace be upon him), on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), that he said:
When the world turns its face toward a person, it grants him the good traits of others, and when it turns away from him, it strips him of his own good traits.
ai.seo_question: What is the effect of worldly favor on a person's character according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this narration from Imam al-Rida (a.s.) elucidates the transient nature of worldly favor (*dunya*) as a test of spiritual authenticity. It highlights how external circumstances can mask or reveal one’s true character, serving as a reminder for believers to anchor their virtues in divine constancy rather than fluctuating worldly status.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 35-9 Al-Hakim Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sowli quoted on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Isma’il, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Al-Abbas that Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) narrated on the authority of his father (a.s.), on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad (a.s.), “
When the world’s affairs run in one’s favor, he even reveals other people’s good traits, but when the world’s affairs run against someone’s favor, he even forgets about his own good traits.”
